title: Dark chocolate peanut butter cups
subtitle: Home-made chocolate cups with a firm peanut butter filling, set in mini muffin cases
excerpt: Home-made peanut butter cups use a two-layer method: a thin base of tempered or simply melted dark chocolate, a peanut butter and icing sugar filling pressed on top, and a chocolate lid. The filling sets to a drier, more fudge-like texture than the commercial version, which is what allows it to be set at room temperature rather than chilled.
sourceNotes: Chocolate peanut butter cups were popularised in the United States in the 1920s, particularly through the Reese's brand. Home versions using dark chocolate and a simplified peanut butter filling became common in UK home-confectionery from the 1990s onwards. The technique documented here uses a direct-melt approach rather than tempering for home accessibility.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in a single layer on a tray until firm, then transfer to a bag. Keep frozen for up to 3 months. Eat from the freezer or allow 10 minutes at room temperature.
recipe.batchNotes: Scale up freely. These make good gifts; a batch of 40 can be made in under an hour.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keep refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks. The chocolate will bloom slightly at room temperature so serve cool.

glossaryTerms.definition: The filling in a home-made peanut butter cup is a dry, fudge-like paste made from peanut butter, icing sugar, and a little butter. The icing sugar absorbs oil from the peanut butter and binds the mixture so it holds its shape at room temperature. The ratio of icing sugar determines the texture: more sugar gives a drier, firmer filling that sets without chilling; less sugar gives a creamier but less stable centre.

content.text: must be stiff enough to hold a disc shape when pressed; if it is too soft it will push the top layer of chocolate aside when you pour it. If the filling feels sticky, work in a little more icing sugar.

items.prepNote: 70% cocoa or higher, broken into pieces
plus flaked sea salt for topping, optional

content.text: Line a mini muffin tin with paper cases. Mix together the peanut butter, sifted icing sugar, softened butter, and salt until you have a stiff, dough-like paste. It should hold its shape when pressed. Set aside.
Melt the chocolate in a metal bowl set over a pan of barely simmering water, stirring until smooth. Remove from heat.
Spoon about 1 teaspoon of melted chocolate into each paper case. Using a small spoon or clean paintbrush, push the chocolate up the sides of each case to form a shell. Chill for 10 minutes until set.

Roll a small piece of peanut butter filling between your palms into a ball, then press it flat into a disc slightly smaller in diameter than the paper case. Press a filling disc into each chocolate shell.

Rewarm the remaining chocolate briefly if it has started to thicken. Spoon a teaspoon of chocolate over the filling in each case, spreading it to the edges to seal the cup. Add a pinch of flaked sea salt to the top if using.
Refrigerate for at least 1 hour until fully set. Remove from the fridge 5 minutes before eating.
